name: Tex
expr: Tex = (Weight in grams × 1000) / Length in meters

name: Denier
expr: Denier = (Weight in grams × 9000) / Length in meters

name: Decitex (dtex)
expr: dtex = (Weight in grams × 10000) / Length in meters

name: Direct System (concept)
expr: concept: mass per unit length — a higher number means a coarser yarn

name: English Cotton Count (Ne)
expr: Ne = Length in yards / (840 × Weight in lb)

name: Metric Count (Nm)
expr: Nm = Length in meters / (1000 × Weight in kg)

name: Worsted Count
expr: Worsted Count = Length in yards / (560 × Weight in lb)

name: Indirect System (concept)
expr: concept: length per unit weight — a higher number means a finer yarn

name: Tex from Ne
expr: Tex = 590.5 / Ne

name: Tex from Nm
expr: Tex = 1000 / Nm

name: Denier from Tex
expr: Denier = Tex × 9

name: Denier from Ne
expr: Denier = 5315 / Ne

name: Ne from Tex
expr: Ne = 590.5 / Tex

name: Nm from Tex
expr: Nm = 1000 / Tex

name: Twist Multiplier (English System)
expr: TM = TPI / √Ne

name: Twist Per Inch (TPI)
expr: TPI = TM × √Ne

name: Twist Per Meter (TPM)
expr: TPM = TPI × 39.37

name: Twist Angle (concept)
expr: tanθ = π × yarn diameter × twist per unit length

name: Mechanical Draft
expr: Draft = Delivered Hank / Fed Hank

name: Draft from Roller Speeds
expr: Draft = Front Roller Surface Speed / Back Roller Surface Speed

name: Actual Draft
expr: Actual Draft = Mechanical Draft × (1 − Slippage%/100)

name: Hank of Sliver/Roving
expr: Hank = Length in yards / (840 × Weight in lb)

name: Delivered Hank in Drafting
expr: Delivered Hank = Fed Hank × Draft

name: Total Draft (Multi-Passage)
expr: Total Draft = Draft₁ × Draft₂ × Draft₃ × ...

name: Doubling (concept)
expr: concept: the number of slivers or rovings fed together into one machine passage to improve evenness

name: Coefficient of Variation (CV%)
expr: CV% = (Standard Deviation / Mean) × 100

name: Unevenness (U%) (concept)
expr: concept: Uster mean deviation of linear density expressed as a percentage of the mean

name: Ring Frame Production (concept)
expr: concept: spindle speed, twist per inch, yarn count, and machine efficiency together determine output per shift

name: Ends Per Inch (EPI) (concept)
expr: concept: number of warp yarns per inch of fabric width — a measure of warp density

name: Picks Per Inch (PPI) (concept)
expr: concept: number of weft yarns per inch of fabric length — a measure of weft density

name: Warp Cover Factor
expr: K_warp = EPI / √Ne(warp)

name: Weft Cover Factor
expr: K_weft = PPI / √Ne(weft)

name: Total Fabric Cover Factor
expr: K_total = K_warp + K_weft − (K_warp × K_weft) / 28

name: Crimp Percentage
expr: Crimp% = ((Yarn Length − Fabric Length) / Fabric Length) × 100

name: Fabric Sett Notation (concept)
expr: concept: fabric construction written as EPI × PPI / Warp Count × Weft Count, e.g. 96 × 72 / 40s × 40s

name: Warp GSM Contribution
expr: GSM(warp) = (EPI × 1.5476 × (100 + Warp Crimp%)) / (Ne(warp) × 100)

name: Weft GSM Contribution
expr: GSM(weft) = (PPI × 1.5476 × (100 + Weft Crimp%)) / (Ne(weft) × 100)

name: Total Fabric GSM
expr: GSM = GSM(warp) + GSM(weft)

name: GSM by Direct Measurement
expr: GSM = Fabric Weight in grams / Fabric Area in m²

name: GSM to Ounces per Square Yard
expr: oz/yd² = GSM × 0.0295

name: Roll Weight
expr: Roll Weight (kg) = GSM × Width (m) × Length (m) / 1000

name: Loom Production Rate
expr: Production (m/min) = Loom RPM / (PPI × 39.37)

name: Loom Production per Shift
expr: Production (m/shift) = (RPM × 60 × Hours × Efficiency%) / (PPI × 39.37 × 100)

name: Loom Efficiency
expr: Efficiency% = (Actual Production / Theoretical Production) × 100

name: Take-up Percentage
expr: Take-up% = ((Yarn Fed Length − Fabric Length Produced) / Yarn Fed Length) × 100

name: Size Add-on Percentage
expr: Add-on% = ((Sized Yarn Weight − Grey Yarn Weight) / Grey Yarn Weight) × 100

name: Warp Breakage Rate (concept)
expr: concept: number of warp yarn breaks per fixed number of picks, used to judge warp and sizing quality

name: Weft Breakage Rate (concept)
expr: concept: number of weft yarn breaks per fixed number of picks, used to judge weft and loom setting quality

name: Stitch Density
expr: Stitch Density = Wales per inch × Courses per inch

name: Loop Length (concept)
expr: concept: the length of yarn consumed to form one knitted loop — controls fabric tightness and GSM

name: Tightness Factor (approx.)
expr: TF ≈ √(Yarn Count in Tex) / Loop Length (mm)

name: Course Length (concept)
expr: concept: total yarn length consumed to knit one complete course across the fabric width

name: Knitted Fabric GSM (concept)
expr: concept: determined by loop length, yarn count, and stitch density together

name: Knitting Machine Production (concept)
expr: concept: machine RPM, number of feeders, and efficiency together determine fabric output per shift

name: Liquor Ratio
expr: Liquor Ratio = Weight of Dye Liquor : Weight of Fabric (e.g. 1:10)

name: Shade Percentage (% owf)
expr: Shade% = (Weight of Dye / Weight of Fabric) × 100

name: Dye Exhaustion Percentage
expr: Exhaustion% = ((Initial Dye Conc. − Final Dye Conc. in Bath) / Initial Dye Conc.) × 100

name: Dye Fixation Percentage
expr: Fixation% = (Dye Fixed on Fabric / Dye Absorbed by Fabric) × 100

name: Wet Pick-up Percentage
expr: Wet Pick-up% = ((Wet Fabric Weight − Dry Fabric Weight) / Dry Fabric Weight) × 100

name: Finishing Add-on Percentage
expr: Add-on% = ((Weight After Treatment − Weight Before Treatment) / Weight Before Treatment) × 100

name: Colour Fastness Grading (concept)
expr: concept: rated on a 1–5 grey-scale for resistance to washing, rubbing, and light exposure

name: Trash Content Percentage
expr: Trash% = (Weight of Trash / Total Sample Weight) × 100

name: Ginning Outturn Percentage (GOT)
expr: GOT% = (Lint Weight / Seed Cotton Weight) × 100

name: Fibre Fineness – Micronaire Value (concept)
expr: concept: an airflow-based index of cotton fibre fineness and maturity, reported in micrograms per inch

name: Staple Length (concept)
expr: concept: the characteristic (average) length of fibres in a cotton sample, a key spinnability indicator

name: Fibre Maturity Ratio (concept)
expr: concept: the proportion of cell-wall thickness to fibre diameter, indicating how fully a cotton fibre has developed

name: Moisture Regain of Fibres (concept)
expr: concept: standard equilibrium moisture regain differs by fibre type, e.g. cotton ≈ 8.5%, wool ≈ 16%

name: Tenacity
expr: Tenacity = Breaking Force / Linear Density (cN/tex or g/tex)

name: Tensile Strength
expr: Tensile Strength = Breaking Load / Cross-sectional Area

name: Elongation Percentage
expr: Elongation% = (Extension at Break / Original Length) × 100

name: Bursting Strength (concept)
expr: concept: the pressure required to rupture a fabric by uniform pressure applied perpendicular to its surface

name: Tear Strength (concept)
expr: concept: the force required to continue or propagate a tear that has already started in a fabric

name: Yarn Strength CV% (concept)
expr: concept: the coefficient of variation of single-yarn breaking strength across test specimens

name: Moisture Regain Percentage
expr: Regain% = ((Wet Weight − Dry Weight) / Dry Weight) × 100

name: Moisture Content Percentage
expr: Moisture Content% = ((Wet Weight − Dry Weight) / Wet Weight) × 100

name: Air Permeability (concept)
expr: concept: the rate of airflow passing perpendicularly through a known fabric area under a fixed pressure difference

name: Wicking Rate (concept)
expr: concept: the rate at which liquid moisture rises through a fabric by capillary action, measured over time

name: Abrasion Resistance – Martindale (concept)
expr: concept: number of rub cycles a fabric withstands before a defined level of surface damage occurs

name: Pilling Resistance Grading (concept)
expr: concept: fabric surface pilling rated on a 1–5 scale after a standard rubbing test, 5 being no pilling

name: Crease Recovery Angle (concept)
expr: concept: the angle to which a folded fabric specimen recovers after release, indicating wrinkle resistance

name: Dimensional Stability / Shrinkage%
expr: Shrinkage% = ((Original Dimension − Dimension After Washing) / Original Dimension) × 100

name: Fabric Cost per Meter (concept)
expr: concept: sum of warp cost, weft cost, and weaving/processing charges, divided by loom efficiency

name: Machine Utilization Percentage
expr: Utilization% = (Actual Running Time / Available Time) × 100

name: Process Waste Percentage
expr: Waste% = (Waste Generated / Total Material Input) × 100

name: Yarn Cost per kg (concept)
expr: concept: raw material cost plus conversion (spinning) cost and overheads, per kilogram of yarn produced

name: Labour Productivity (concept)
expr: concept: output produced (in meters, kg, or pieces) per worker per shift

name: Basis Weight (concept)
expr: concept: mass per unit area of a nonwoven fabric, reported in GSM, same principle as woven fabric weight

name: Fibre Orientation Index (concept)
expr: concept: a measure of how aligned fibres are within a nonwoven web, affecting strength in different directions

name: Bonding Efficiency (concept)
expr: concept: the degree to which thermal, chemical, or mechanical bonding holds fibres together in a nonwoven web

name: Cotton Fibre Length Classification (concept)
expr: concept: cotton staple grouped as short (<24mm), medium (24-26mm), long (27-32mm), and extra-long (>32mm)

name: Cotton Micronaire Value (concept)
expr: concept: an airflow-based index of fibre fineness and maturity, ideal range roughly 3.5-4.9

name: Cotton Moisture Regain (Standard)
expr: Standard Regain = 8.5% at 65% RH and 20°C

name: Cotton Fibre Bundle Strength (concept)
expr: concept: breaking tenacity of a bundle of fibres, measured in g/tex via HVI, typically 25-30 g/tex

name: Cotton Grade Classification (concept)
expr: concept: cotton graded by colour, trash content, and preparation into grades such as Good, Middling, and Strict Low Middling

name: Short Fibre Content Percentage
expr: SFC% = (Weight of fibres shorter than 12.7mm / Total sample weight) × 100

name: Cotton Uniformity Index (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of mean fibre length to upper-half mean length, expressed as a percentage

name: Cotton Colour Grade – Reflectance (Rd)
expr: concept: Rd measures the brightness/greyness of cotton on the Nickerson-Hunter colour chart

name: Cotton Colour Grade – Yellowness (+b)
expr: concept: +b measures the degree of yellowness of cotton fibre on the Nickerson-Hunter colour chart

name: Cotton Ginning Efficiency (concept)
expr: concept: the rate at which a gin separates lint from seed cotton without fibre damage

name: Cotton Lint Percentage
expr: Lint% = (Lint Weight / Seed Cotton Weight) × 100

name: Cotton Seed Index (concept)
expr: concept: the weight in grams of 100 cotton seeds, used to judge seed and variety quality

name: Cotton Fibre Maturity Percentage
expr: Maturity% = (Number of Mature Fibres / Total Fibres Examined) × 100

name: Cotton Neps per Gram (concept)
expr: concept: the number of small fibre entanglements (neps) counted per gram of cotton or sliver

name: Cotton Elongation at Break (concept)
expr: concept: cotton fibre typically elongates 6-10% of its length before breaking

name: Cotton Fibre Fineness (Denier, Direct)
expr: Fineness (mtex) = Weight in mg / Length in meters × 1000

name: Cotton Bale Density (concept)
expr: concept: mass of compressed cotton per unit volume of a bale, affecting storage and transport cost

name: Cotton Moisture Content at Ginning (concept)
expr: concept: seed cotton moisture is controlled before ginning to reduce fibre and seed damage

name: HVI Span Length (concept)
expr: concept: the distance spanned by a specified percentage of fibres in a High Volume Instrument test, e.g. 2.5% span length

name: Cotton Trash Particle Count (concept)
expr: concept: number of visible trash particles per unit area, used alongside trash percentage for grading

name: Cotton Fibre Diameter (concept)
expr: concept: the average cross-sectional diameter of a cotton fibre, typically 12-22 micrometers

name: Cotton Wax Content Percentage (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of natural wax on raw cotton fibre surface, removed during scouring

name: Cotton Pectin Content (concept)
expr: concept: natural cementing substance in the cotton fibre wall, largely removed during scouring

name: Cellulose Content of Cotton (concept)
expr: concept: mature cotton fibre is approximately 88-96% cellulose by weight

name: Cotton Crimp (Convolutions) (concept)
expr: concept: natural twist-like ribbon structure along the cotton fibre length that aids inter-fibre cohesion in spinning

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Fibre Diameter (Micron)
expr: Fineness is expressed directly as average fibre diameter in microns (μm)

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Fineness – Bradford (Worsted) Count (concept)
expr: concept: an indirect count historically used to grade wool fineness, higher count meaning finer wool

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Crimp Frequency (concept)
expr: concept: number of natural waves (crimps) per unit length of wool fibre, related to fineness and elasticity

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Standard Moisture Regain
expr: Standard Regain = 16% at 65% RH and 20°C

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Yield Percentage
expr: Yield% = (Clean Wool Weight / Greasy Wool Weight) × 100

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Grease (Lanolin) Content Percentage
expr: Grease% = (Weight of Grease Removed / Original Greasy Wool Weight) × 100

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Staple Length (concept)
expr: concept: the natural length of a lock of wool fibres as sheared, a key sorting criterion

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Wool Medullation Percentage (concept)
expr: concept: the proportion of wool fibres containing a hollow medulla, affecting dyeability and handle

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Silk Denier (Raw Silk)
expr: Silk is numbered on the direct Denier system: Denier = (Weight in g × 9000) / Length in m

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Silk Degumming Loss Percentage
expr: Degumming Loss% = ((Weight Before Degumming − Weight After) / Weight Before) × 100

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Silk Sericin Content (concept)
expr: concept: raw silk contains roughly 20-30% sericin gum, removed during degumming to reveal lustrous fibroin fibre

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Silk Reelability (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of a cocoon's filament that can be successfully reeled without breaking

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Silk Filament Length (concept)
expr: concept: the continuous length of filament that can be unwound from a single silkworm cocoon, often 300-900m

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Jute Fibre Fineness
expr: Jute fineness is expressed in Tex: Tex = (Weight in g × 1000) / Length in m

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Bast Fibre Extraction Yield Percentage
expr: Yield% = (Extracted Fibre Weight / Stem Weight) × 100

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Retting Process (concept)
expr: concept: microbial or chemical process that breaks down the pectin binding bast fibres to the stem, enabling extraction

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Jute Batching Oil Add-on Percentage
expr: Add-on% = (Weight of Batching Oil Applied / Dry Fibre Weight) × 100

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Flax Fibre Fineness (concept)
expr: concept: flax (linen) fineness is commonly expressed using the Lea or Metric count system

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Coir Fibre Properties (concept)
expr: concept: coconut husk fibre is coarse, highly lignified, and valued for durability and moisture resistance

cat: Natural Fibres – Wool, Silk & Bast Fibres
name: Standard Moisture Regain of Common Fibres (concept)
expr: concept: jute ≈ 13.75%, flax ≈ 12%, silk ≈ 11%, wool ≈ 16%, cotton ≈ 8.5%

name: Denier Per Filament (DPF)
expr: DPF = Total Yarn Denier / Number of Filaments

name: Draw Ratio (Synthetic Fibre)
expr: Draw Ratio = Length After Drawing / Length Before Drawing

name: Filament Crimp Percentage (Texturizing)
expr: Crimp% = ((Uncrimped Length − Crimped Length) / Uncrimped Length) × 100

name: Spandex Elastic Recovery Percentage
expr: Recovery% = (Recovered Extension / Applied Extension) × 100

name: Viscose Degree of Polymerization (concept)
expr: concept: the average number of glucose units in a cellulose chain, influencing viscose fibre strength

name: Lyocell (NMMO) Solvent Spinning (concept)
expr: concept: a closed-loop process dissolving cellulose directly in an amine-oxide solvent to spin fibre without derivatization

name: Modal Fibre Wet Modulus (concept)
expr: concept: a measure of a regenerated fibre's resistance to stretching while wet, higher than standard viscose

name: Polyester Intrinsic Viscosity (concept)
expr: concept: a measure of polymer chain length in polyester chips, correlating with fibre strength and processability

name: Nylon Relative Viscosity (concept)
expr: concept: a measure of nylon polymer molecular weight, tested by comparing polymer solution flow time to solvent

name: Melt Flow Index (concept)
expr: concept: the mass of polymer melt extruded through a die in 10 minutes under standard load, indicating melt viscosity

name: Glass Transition Temperature (Tg) (concept)
expr: concept: the temperature at which an amorphous polymer changes from a rigid glassy state to a flexible rubbery state

name: Melting Temperature (Tm) (concept)
expr: concept: the temperature at which the crystalline regions of a synthetic fibre polymer melt

name: Spinneret Hole Count (concept)
expr: concept: the number of extrusion holes in a spinneret, determining the number of filaments produced per spin position

name: Filament Denier Uniformity (concept)
expr: concept: consistency of individual filament denier across a multi-filament yarn, affecting dye uptake evenness

name: Bicomponent Fibre Ratio (concept)
expr: concept: the volume or weight ratio of two polymer components co-extruded within a single fibre, e.g. sheath-core

name: Acrylic Fibre Wet-Spinning (concept)
expr: concept: acrylic fibre is typically produced by extruding polymer solution into a coagulation bath rather than melt spinning

name: Polypropylene Fibre Density (concept)
expr: concept: polypropylene has one of the lowest densities among common textile fibres, around 0.91 g/cm³

name: Man-Made Fibre Tenacity Range (concept)
expr: concept: typical dry tenacity ranges from about 3-6 g/den for regenerated fibres and 4-9 g/den for high-tenacity synthetics

name: Synthetic Fibre Shrinkage in Hot Water (concept)
expr: concept: percentage dimensional change of a fibre or yarn sample after immersion in hot water at a fixed temperature and time

name: Texturizing – False Twist Method (concept)
expr: concept: a filament yarn is twisted, heat-set, and untwisted to impart durable crimp and bulk

name: Air-Jet Texturizing (concept)
expr: concept: turbulent air entangles filaments to create loops and bulk without applying heat-set twist

name: Draw-Texturizing Speed vs Denier (concept)
expr: concept: higher texturizing speeds generally require adjustments to draw ratio to maintain target yarn denier

name: Recycled Polyester (rPET) Fibre (concept)
expr: concept: polyester fibre produced by depolymerizing and re-extruding recovered PET, e.g. from bottles

name: Fibre Blend Ratio
expr: Blend Ratio% = (Weight of Fibre A / Total Blend Weight) × 100

name: Blend Regain (Mixed Fibres) (concept)
expr: concept: the effective moisture regain of a fibre blend is the weighted average of each component's standard regain

name: Burning Test (concept)
expr: concept: identifies a fibre by observing its flame behaviour, odor, and residue when burned

name: Solubility Test (concept)
expr: concept: identifies a fibre by its characteristic dissolving or resistance in specific chemical reagents

name: Microscopic Longitudinal View (concept)
expr: concept: identifies natural fibres by characteristic surface features seen lengthwise under a microscope, e.g. cotton's twisted ribbon shape

name: Microscopic Cross-Section View (concept)
expr: concept: identifies fibres by their characteristic cross-sectional shape, e.g. cotton's kidney bean shape, wool's near-circular shape

name: Fibre Density (Specific Gravity) (concept)
expr: concept: fibre identity can be indicated by density, e.g. cotton ≈1.54, polyester ≈1.38, nylon ≈1.14 g/cm³

name: Refractive Index of Fibres (concept)
expr: concept: fibres can be identified by comparing their refractive index against index-matching liquids under a microscope

name: Staining Test (concept)
expr: concept: fibres absorb standardized multi-fibre stains differently, allowing rapid visual identification of blends

name: Fibre Diameter Measurement (Projection Microscope) (concept)
expr: concept: fibre diameter is measured optically by projecting a magnified fibre image onto a calibrated screen

name: Fibre Tenacity Test (concept)
expr: concept: single-fibre tensile testing measures breaking force and elongation to characterize strength and identify fibre type

name: Melting Point Test (concept)
expr: concept: synthetic fibres can be identified by their characteristic melting point observed on a hot-stage microscope

name: Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) Identification (concept)
expr: concept: identifies fibre polymer type from its characteristic infrared absorption spectrum

name: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) (concept)
expr: concept: measures heat flow to determine a fibre's glass transition, crystallization, and melting temperatures

name: Moisture Regain Test (Oven-Dry Method)
expr: Regain% = ((Original Weight − Oven-Dry Weight) / Oven-Dry Weight) × 100

name: Conditioned Weight (concept)
expr: concept: fibre or yarn weight measured after equilibrating at standard atmospheric conditions (65% RH, 20°C)

name: Standard Testing Atmosphere (concept)
expr: concept: textile testing is standardized at 65% ± 2% relative humidity and 20°C ± 2°C for comparable results

name: Fibre Count per Cross-Section (Yarn) (concept)
expr: concept: the approximate number of fibres in a yarn's cross-section, estimated from yarn linear density and fibre fineness

name: Number of Fibres in Yarn Cross-Section
expr: N = Yarn Tex / Fibre Tex

name: Fibre Length Distribution (concept)
expr: concept: a histogram showing the proportion of fibres at each length class within a sample

name: Fibre Bundle Tenacity vs Single Fibre Tenacity (concept)
expr: concept: bundle tests average many fibres at once and are faster, while single-fibre tests give more precise individual strength values

name: Wet vs Dry Strength Ratio (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of a fibre's breaking strength wet to its strength dry, cotton gains strength wet while many synthetics lose some

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Blow Room Line Efficiency
expr: Efficiency% = (Actual Output / Theoretical Output) × 100

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Blow Room Cleaning Efficiency
expr: Cleaning Efficiency% = (Trash Removed / Trash Present in Raw Material) × 100

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Lap Weight per Meter (concept)
expr: concept: the mass per unit length of the compressed fibre sheet (lap) produced at the end of the blow room line

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Blow Room Waste Extraction Percentage
expr: Waste% = (Waste Extracted / Input Material Weight) × 100

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Opening & Cleaning Points (concept)
expr: concept: successive beater and grid-bar stages in the blow room progressively open tufts and remove trash

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Carding Production Rate (concept)
expr: concept: card output depends on cylinder speed, doffer speed, and sliver hank, expressed in kg per hour

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Carding Draft
expr: Card Draft = Delivered Sliver Hank / Fed Lap Hank

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Card Waste Percentage
expr: Card Waste% = (Waste Extracted at Card / Input Material Weight) × 100

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Neps per Gram of Sliver (concept)
expr: concept: number of fibre entanglements counted per gram of card or comber sliver, a key evenness indicator

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Doffer Speed vs Delivery Rate (concept)
expr: concept: doffer speed largely determines the linear delivery rate of card sliver for a given sliver hank

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Cylinder-to-Doffer Speed Ratio (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of cylinder to doffer surface speed influences fibre transfer efficiency and web quality

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Licker-in Speed (concept)
expr: concept: the rotational speed of the licker-in roller controls initial fibre opening and short fibre/trash removal

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Combing Noil Percentage
expr: Noil% = (Noil Weight Removed / Total Fed Sliver Weight) × 100

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Comber Efficiency (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of actual comber production to theoretical production at rated nips per minute

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Nips per Minute (Comber) (concept)
expr: concept: the number of combing cycles the comber performs each minute, setting the maximum production rate

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Lap Preparation for Combing (concept)
expr: concept: sliver laps or sliver-fed systems are prepared to feed the comber with uniform, well-aligned fibre tufts

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Draw Frame Total Draft
expr: Total Draft = Fed Sliver Hank Combined / Delivered Sliver Hank

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Number of Doublings (Drawing)
expr: Doublings = Number of Slivers Fed Together at the Draw Frame

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Autoleveller Correction (concept)
expr: concept: an autoleveller measures incoming sliver thickness and adjusts drafting in real time to even out the output sliver

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Sliver Evenness Improvement via Doubling (concept)
expr: concept: doubling several slivers together statistically reduces overall linear-density variation in the blended sliver

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Simplex (Roving Frame) Twist Multiplier (concept)
expr: concept: roving twist multiplier is kept lower than final yarn TM to allow easy drafting at the ring frame

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Roving Bobbin Build (Cone Angle) (concept)
expr: concept: the tapered shape wound onto a roving bobbin to allow smooth unwinding during ring spinning

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Flyer Speed vs Roving Production (concept)
expr: concept: flyer rotational speed, together with roving hank and machine efficiency, determines roving output rate

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Roving Hank
expr: Roving Hank = Length in yards / (840 × Weight in lb)

cat: Spinning Preparatory – Blow Room, Carding & Combing
name: Preparatory Process Sequence (concept)
expr: concept: typical short-staple spinning sequence is blow room → carding → (combing) → drawing → simplex → ring spinning

name: Spindle Speed vs Yarn Production (concept)
expr: concept: higher spindle RPM increases yarn output but is limited by yarn tension and end-breakage rate

name: Ring Frame Efficiency
expr: Efficiency% = (Actual Production / Theoretical Production) × 100

name: Traveler Speed (concept)
expr: concept: the ring traveler orbits the ring at a speed close to spindle speed, inserting twist as it winds yarn onto the bobbin

name: End Breakage Rate (Ring Spinning)
expr: Breakage Rate = Number of Yarn Breaks / (1000 Spindle-Hours)

name: Ring Frame Production per Spindle (concept)
expr: concept: output per spindle depends on spindle speed, twist per inch, yarn count, and running efficiency

name: Balloon Control Ring (concept)
expr: concept: a small ring placed above the main ring to control excessive yarn balloon during high-speed spinning

name: Cop Build (Ring Bobbin) (concept)
expr: concept: the shape formed as yarn winds onto the ring bobbin, controlled by the ring rail's traverse motion

name: Rotor Speed vs Yarn Count (concept)
expr: concept: for a given rotor diameter, achievable rotor speed is limited more for finer counts due to yarn tension

name: Open-End (Rotor) Production Rate (concept)
expr: concept: rotor yarn output depends on rotor speed, yarn count, and machine efficiency, generally higher than ring spinning

name: Rotor Spinning Twist Factor (concept)
expr: concept: open-end yarns typically require a higher twist factor than ring yarns for comparable strength

name: Fibre-to-Yarn Ratio in OE Spinning (concept)
expr: concept: the wrapping and core fibre arrangement characteristic of rotor-spun yarn structure

name: Navel Type (Rotor Spinning) (concept)
expr: concept: the yarn-forming navel shape and material affect yarn hairiness and handle in rotor spinning

name: Air-Jet Spinning Speed (concept)
expr: concept: air-jet (vortex) spinning achieves very high delivery speeds by using swirling air to insert false twist

name: Friction (DREF) Spinning Production (concept)
expr: concept: friction spinning suits coarse, bulky yarns and is not generally suited to fine counts

name: Yarn Hairiness Index (concept)
expr: concept: a measure (e.g. H-value) of the total length of protruding fibre ends and loops per unit yarn length

name: Yarn Imperfections (Thin/Thick/Neps) (concept)
expr: concept: Uster testing counts thin places, thick places, and neps per kilometer of yarn against reference thresholds

name: Ring vs Rotor Yarn Structure (concept)
expr: concept: ring yarn has a compact, parallel-fibre structure while rotor yarn has a wrapped, bulkier structure

name: Spinning Triangle (concept)
expr: concept: the small triangular zone at the front roller nip in ring spinning where fibres converge before twist is inserted

name: Compact Spinning (concept)
expr: concept: uses a condensing zone after the front roller to narrow the spinning triangle, reducing hairiness

name: Siro Spinning (concept)
expr: concept: two separately fed roving strands are twisted together at the front roller to form a yarn resembling a two-ply yarn

name: Winding Efficiency
expr: Efficiency% = (Actual Winding Production / Theoretical Production) × 100

name: Clearer Cut Rate (concept)
expr: concept: the number of yarn faults removed per unit length by an electronic yarn clearer during winding

name: Package Density (Cone/Cheese) (concept)
expr: concept: the mass of yarn wound per unit volume of a cone or cheese package, affecting dye penetration

name: Splice Strength Retention (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of original yarn strength retained at a spliced joint compared to unspliced yarn

name: Warping Efficiency (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of actual warp beam production to theoretical production during the warping process

name: Number of Ends in a Warp Beam (concept)
expr: concept: determined by the fabric's total ends required divided among the number of beams used at the loom

name: Creel Capacity (concept)
expr: concept: the number of yarn packages a warping creel can hold and feed simultaneously

name: Warp Beam Density (concept)
expr: concept: the mass of yarn wound per unit length of a warp beam, affecting beam diameter and let-off tension

name: Sectional Warping (concept)
expr: concept: warp sections are wound side by side onto a drum, then transferred together onto the weaver's beam

name: Direct (Beam) Warping (concept)
expr: concept: all ends are wound directly and simultaneously from a full creel onto the final warp beam

name: Sizing Add-on Percentage
expr: Add-on% = ((Sized Yarn Weight − Grey Yarn Weight) / Grey Yarn Weight) × 100

name: Stretch Percentage in Sizing
expr: Stretch% = ((Delivered Length − Fed Length) / Fed Length) × 100

name: Size Paste Viscosity (concept)
expr: concept: the flow resistance of the size paste, controlled to ensure uniform yarn coating without excess pick-up

name: Size Paste Concentration (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of sizing agent solids in the size bath, adjusted for yarn count and desired add-on

name: Drying Efficiency in Sizing (concept)
expr: concept: the effectiveness of the drying cylinders in removing moisture from sized yarn before beaming

name: Sized Yarn Moisture Content (concept)
expr: concept: residual moisture left in yarn after the sizing drying section, checked to avoid mildew or sticking

name: Size Recipe Selection (concept)
expr: concept: sizing agent choice (starch, PVA, acrylic) depends on yarn type, count, and downstream desizing method

name: Warp Breakage Reduction via Sizing (concept)
expr: concept: adequate sizing add-on reduces hairiness and increases yarn smoothness, lowering warp breaks on the loom

name: Beam-to-Beam Tension Uniformity (concept)
expr: concept: consistent tension across all warp beams at the loom ensures even fabric appearance and reduces defects

name: Two-for-One (TFO) Twisting (concept)
expr: concept: a doubling/twisting process that inserts two turns of twist per revolution of the spindle, doubling productivity

name: Doubling (Plying) Twist Direction (concept)
expr: concept: single yarns are typically S-twisted and plied with Z-twist, or vice versa, to balance the final yarn

name: Ply Yarn Count
expr: Resultant Count (Ne) = 1 / (1/Ne₁ + 1/Ne₂ + ... )

name: Shedding Motion (concept)
expr: concept: raises and lowers warp yarns to form the shed through which the weft is inserted

name: Picking Motion (concept)
expr: concept: propels the weft (filling) yarn across the shed from one side of the loom to the other

name: Beating-up Motion (concept)
expr: concept: the reed pushes the newly inserted weft pick firmly against the already-woven fabric fell

name: Take-up Motion (concept)
expr: concept: winds the woven fabric forward at a controlled rate to set picks per inch

name: Let-off Motion (concept)
expr: concept: releases warp yarn from the warp beam at a controlled rate and tension as weaving proceeds

name: Warp Protection Motion (concept)
expr: concept: stops the loom automatically if excessive warp tension or a warp break is detected

name: Weft Protection Motion (concept)
expr: concept: stops the loom automatically if the weft yarn breaks or runs out during picking

name: Temple (Fabric Width Control) (concept)
expr: concept: a device holding the fabric at full width near the fell to prevent weft-way shrinkage during weaving

name: Heald (Heddle) Frame Motion (concept)
expr: concept: heald frames carry warp yarns and are raised/lowered by the shedding mechanism to form the weave pattern

name: Reed Count (concept)
expr: concept: the number of dents (gaps) per unit width of the reed, directly influencing achievable ends per inch

name: Reed Space (concept)
expr: concept: the usable width of the reed available for the warp sheet, setting the maximum fabric width

name: Pick Insertion Rate
expr: Picks Inserted per Minute = Loom RPM (for single-pick-per-cycle looms)

name: Loom Timing Diagram (concept)
expr: concept: shows the angular relationship between shedding, picking, and beating events over one loom cycle

name: Positive vs Negative Let-off (concept)
expr: concept: positive let-off drives the beam mechanically at a set rate, while negative let-off releases warp under spring/weight tension

name: Cam (Tappet) Shedding (concept)
expr: concept: uses rotating cams to raise and lower heald frames, suited to simple weaves with limited repeats

name: Dobby Shedding (concept)
expr: concept: controls a larger number of heald frames individually via a pattern chain or electronic program

name: Jacquard Shedding (concept)
expr: concept: controls individual warp threads (not frames) allowing intricate, large-repeat figured designs

name: Loom Speed – Picks per Minute (concept)
expr: concept: the maximum sustainable insertion rate of a loom, higher for shuttleless systems than shuttle looms

name: Weft Insertion Rate (m/min) (concept)
expr: concept: total length of weft inserted per minute, calculated as PPM × fabric width, used to compare loom types

name: Fell of the Cloth (concept)
expr: concept: the line where the last inserted weft pick meets the already-formed fabric

name: Shuttle Loom (concept)
expr: concept: inserts weft by passing a shuttle carrying a weft pirn through the shed, relatively slow and noisy

name: Air-Jet Loom (concept)
expr: concept: inserts weft using a jet of compressed air, suited to high-speed weaving of lighter fabrics

name: Water-Jet Loom (concept)
expr: concept: inserts weft using a jet of water, suited to hydrophobic filament yarns like polyester and nylon

name: Rapier Loom (concept)
expr: concept: inserts weft using rigid or flexible rapier arms that carry the yarn across the shed

name: Projectile Loom (concept)
expr: concept: inserts weft using a small gripper projectile that carries the yarn across the shed on guide teeth

name: Loom Type Comparison – Speed (concept)
expr: concept: shuttleless looms (air-jet, rapier, projectile) generally achieve much higher pick insertion rates than shuttle looms

name: Plain Weave (concept)
expr: concept: the simplest interlacement where each weft pick alternates over and under successive warp ends

name: Twill Weave (concept)
expr: concept: produces a diagonal line effect by progressively offsetting the interlacement point in each successive pick

name: Satin Weave (concept)
expr: concept: uses widely spaced, non-adjacent interlacement points to create a smooth, lustrous fabric surface

name: Weave Repeat Size (concept)
expr: concept: the minimum number of ends and picks needed before the interlacement pattern repeats itself

name: Twill Weave Angle (concept)
expr: concept: the angle of the diagonal twill line, influenced by the relative EPI and PPI of the fabric

name: Dobby Weave (concept)
expr: concept: small, geometric figured patterns woven using a dobby shedding mechanism with limited heald frames

name: Jacquard Weave (concept)
expr: concept: large, intricate figured patterns (e.g. brocade, damask) woven with individual warp-thread control

name: Pile Weave (concept)
expr: concept: an extra set of warp or weft yarns forms raised loops or cut tufts on the fabric surface, e.g. velvet, terry

name: Terry Pile Height (concept)
expr: concept: controlled by the loop-forming warp's slack feed relative to the ground warp during pile weaving

name: Leno Weave (concept)
expr: concept: adjacent warp ends are twisted around each other between weft picks to create an open, stable mesh fabric

name: Honeycomb (Waffle) Weave (concept)
expr: concept: a derivative weave creating raised and depressed cells that give a three-dimensional, absorbent surface

name: Basket Weave (concept)
expr: concept: a plain-weave variation where two or more warp and weft yarns are woven as one, giving a checkerboard look

name: Extra Warp/Weft Figuring (concept)
expr: concept: additional yarn sets beyond the ground weave are used to add surface pattern or texture

name: Weave Diagram (Point Paper Design) (concept)
expr: concept: a grid representation showing which warp ends are raised or lowered for each weft pick in a repeat

name: Fabric Face and Back Distinction (concept)
expr: concept: twill and satin weaves typically show a different appearance on face versus back due to float distribution

name: Float Length (Weave) (concept)
expr: concept: the number of consecutive warp or weft yarns passing over or under the opposite set without interlacing

name: Balanced vs Unbalanced Weave (concept)
expr: concept: a balanced weave has similar warp and weft yarn count and density, while an unbalanced weave favors one direction

name: Plain (Single) Jersey Structure (concept)
expr: concept: the simplest weft-knit structure, made entirely of knit stitches, curls at the edges and has a distinct face/back

name: Rib Knit Structure (concept)
expr: concept: alternating knit and purl wales on both needle beds, producing a highly extensible, non-curling fabric

name: Interlock Structure (concept)
expr: concept: two interlocking rib structures combined, giving a thicker, more stable, reversible fabric

name: Purl Structure (concept)
expr: concept: alternating knit and purl courses producing a fabric that looks the same on both faces and has high stretch

name: Knitting Machine Gauge (concept)
expr: concept: the number of needles per unit width (e.g. per inch) of the knitting machine cylinder or bed

name: Stitch Density
expr: Stitch Density = Wales per Inch × Courses per Inch

name: Loop Length (concept)
expr: concept: the length of yarn consumed in forming one knitted loop, the primary factor controlling knit fabric tightness

name: Tightness Factor (approx.)
expr: TF ≈ √(Yarn Count in Tex) / Loop Length (mm)

name: Course Length (concept)
expr: concept: the total yarn length consumed to knit one complete course across the fabric width

name: Knitted Fabric GSM (concept)
expr: concept: determined jointly by loop length, yarn linear density, and stitch (wale/course) density

name: Knitting Machine Production Rate (concept)
expr: concept: depends on machine RPM, number of feeders, and running efficiency, expressed in kg or meters per shift

name: Number of Feeders (concept)
expr: concept: the number of yarn feeding points around a circular knitting machine, more feeders raise potential output

name: Yarn Consumption per Unit Area (Knitting) (concept)
expr: concept: total yarn length needed per square meter of knitted fabric, based on loop length and stitch density

name: Spirality (Knit Fabric) (concept)
expr: concept: the angular distortion of wales relative to a straight line, related to yarn twist liveliness

name: Knit Fabric Shrinkage – Relaxation (concept)
expr: concept: dimensional change a knitted fabric undergoes as internal stresses relax after knitting, washing, or drying

name: Tricot Knitting (concept)
expr: concept: a warp-knitting technique producing fine, closely spaced vertical wales with good run resistance

name: Raschel Knitting (concept)
expr: concept: a warp-knitting technique capable of coarser, patterned, and net-like or lace-like structures

name: Warp Knit Run Resistance (concept)
expr: concept: warp-knit fabrics resist unraveling ('running') far better than weft-knit fabrics due to their loop interlocking pattern

name: Number of Guide Bars (Warp Knitting) (concept)
expr: concept: each guide bar in a warp-knitting machine feeds one set of warp yarns, more bars allow more complex structures

name: Weft Insertion in Warp Knitting (concept)
expr: concept: straight-laid weft yarns are inserted and locked in by the warp-knitting stitches to add stability or bulk

name: Seamless Knitting (concept)
expr: concept: garments are knitted to shape on circular machines, minimizing or eliminating cut-and-sew seams

name: Knit Fabric Bursting Strength (concept)
expr: concept: knitted fabrics are typically tested for bursting strength rather than tensile strength due to high extensibility

name: Basis Weight (Nonwoven) (concept)
expr: concept: mass per unit area of a nonwoven fabric, reported in GSM, following the same principle as woven fabric weight

name: Needle Punching (concept)
expr: concept: barbed needles mechanically entangle a fibre web to bond it into a cohesive nonwoven fabric

name: Needle Punch Density (concept)
expr: concept: the number of needle penetrations per unit area of web, affecting nonwoven strength and density

name: Spunbond Process (concept)
expr: concept: continuous filaments are extruded, drawn, and laid directly into a web that is then bonded, typically thermally

name: Meltblown Process (concept)
expr: concept: high-velocity hot air attenuates extruded polymer into very fine microfibres collected as a web

name: SMS (Spunbond-Meltblown-Spunbond) Structure (concept)
expr: concept: a layered nonwoven combining strong spunbond outer layers with a fine-filtering meltblown core

name: Hydroentanglement (Spunlace) (concept)
expr: concept: high-pressure water jets entangle fibres in a web to bond it without adhesives or heat

name: Thermal Bonding (Nonwoven) (concept)
expr: concept: heat and pressure (e.g. calender rolls) fuse thermoplastic fibres or binder fibres to bond the web

name: Chemical (Resin) Bonding (concept)
expr: concept: a liquid or foam binder is applied to a fibre web and cured to bond fibres together

name: Nonwoven Air Permeability (concept)
expr: concept: airflow rate through a nonwoven fabric under fixed pressure, important for filtration and hygiene products

name: Nonwoven Pore Size Distribution (concept)
expr: concept: the range of pore sizes within a nonwoven structure, critical for filtration and barrier performance

name: Carded Web Formation (concept)
expr: concept: staple fibres are opened and aligned by carding rollers to form a uniform web before bonding

name: Airlaid Web Formation (concept)
expr: concept: fibres are dispersed and deposited by an air stream to form a randomly oriented web, common in absorbent products

name: Wetlaid Nonwoven Process (concept)
expr: concept: fibres are dispersed in water and deposited on a moving screen, similar in principle to papermaking

name: Nonwoven Tensile Strength – MD vs CD (concept)
expr: concept: nonwoven strength is measured separately in the machine direction (MD) and cross direction (CD) due to anisotropy

name: Geotextile Nonwoven Properties (concept)
expr: concept: nonwoven geotextiles are engineered for permittivity, puncture resistance, and long-term durability in soil applications

name: Filtration Efficiency (Nonwoven) (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of particles of a given size removed by a nonwoven filter media in a single pass

name: Nonwoven Basis Weight Uniformity (concept)
expr: concept: consistency of mass per unit area across a nonwoven roll, affecting strength and appearance uniformity

name: Desizing Efficiency
expr: Desizing Efficiency% = (Size Removed / Size Originally Applied) × 100

name: Enzymatic Desizing (concept)
expr: concept: amylase enzymes break down starch-based size into soluble sugars that are washed out of the fabric

name: Acid Desizing (concept)
expr: concept: dilute acid hydrolyzes starch size on the fabric, followed by thorough washing

name: Oxidative Desizing (concept)
expr: concept: oxidizing agents degrade size material chemically, suited to synthetic sizing agents like PVA

name: Residual Size Test (TEGEWA Rating) (concept)
expr: concept: an iodine-based spot test rating residual starch size on fabric from 1 (none) to 8 (heavy)

name: Scouring Loss Percentage
expr: Scouring Loss% = ((Weight Before Scouring − Weight After) / Weight Before) × 100

name: Wax and Impurity Removal (Scouring) (concept)
expr: concept: alkaline scouring removes natural waxes, oils, pectin, and other non-cellulosic impurities from raw fabric

name: Wetting Time (Absorbency Test) (concept)
expr: concept: the time for a water drop to fully absorb into a fabric, used to judge scouring effectiveness

name: Alkali Concentration in Scouring (concept)
expr: concept: caustic soda or soda ash concentration in the scouring bath is set according to fibre type and impurity level

name: Whiteness Index (concept)
expr: concept: a numerical value derived from reflectance measurements describing how visually white a bleached fabric appears

name: Degree of Bleaching (concept)
expr: concept: the extent of natural colouring matter removed from fibre, judged by whiteness index and residual yellowness

name: Residual Hydrogen Peroxide Test (concept)
expr: concept: confirms complete neutralization of bleaching agent before subsequent dyeing to avoid shade defects

name: Residual Chlorine Test (concept)
expr: concept: confirms complete removal of chlorine-based bleach residues that could cause fibre damage or yellowing

name: Bleach Bath Stabilizer (concept)
expr: concept: stabilizers control the decomposition rate of hydrogen peroxide to prevent fibre damage during bleaching

name: Mercerization (concept)
expr: concept: treating cotton with concentrated caustic soda under tension to increase lustre, strength, and dye affinity

name: Caustic Concentration in Mercerizing (concept)
expr: concept: mercerizing typically uses 18-25% NaOH solution, with concentration affecting the degree of fibre swelling

name: Tension During Mercerizing (concept)
expr: concept: fabric or yarn is held under tension during mercerizing to preserve fibre alignment and maximize lustre gain

name: Barium Activity Number (concept)
expr: concept: a test comparing barium hydroxide absorption of mercerized versus unmercerized cotton to quantify mercerization degree

name: Causticizing (Yarn Mercerizing) (concept)
expr: concept: mercerization applied to yarn (in hank or package form) before or instead of fabric mercerizing

name: Combined Preparatory Sequence (concept)
expr: concept: typical cotton preparation sequence is desizing → scouring → bleaching → (mercerizing) before dyeing or printing

name: Reactive Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: form a covalent bond with cellulose fibre, giving good wash fastness, widely used for cotton

name: Disperse Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: fine, water-insoluble dye particles dispersed in the dye bath, used mainly for polyester

name: Vat Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: applied in a reduced, water-soluble (leuco) form and then oxidized back to an insoluble pigment inside the fibre

name: Acid Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: applied from an acidic bath, forming ionic bonds mainly with protein fibres like wool and silk, and nylon

name: Basic (Cationic) Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: bond with anionic sites in fibres such as acrylic, giving very bright, intense shades

name: Direct Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: applied directly to cellulosic fibres from a neutral or slightly alkaline bath without a mordant

name: Sulphur Dyes (concept)
expr: concept: economical dyes for cotton giving mainly dark shades, applied in a reduced form similar to vat dyes

name: Shade Percentage (% owf)
expr: Shade% = (Weight of Dye / Weight of Fabric) × 100

name: Dye Exhaustion Percentage
expr: Exhaustion% = ((Initial Dye Concentration − Final Dye Concentration in Bath) / Initial Dye Concentration) × 100

name: Dye Fixation Percentage
expr: Fixation% = (Dye Fixed on Fabric / Dye Absorbed by Fabric) × 100

name: Jigger Dyeing (concept)
expr: concept: fabric in open-width rope form is passed back and forth through a stationary dye bath between two rollers

name: Jet Dyeing (concept)
expr: concept: fabric rope is circulated through a dye bath by a jet of liquor, suited to knitted and delicate fabrics

name: Package Dyeing (concept)
expr: concept: yarn wound on perforated packages (cones/cheeses) is dyed by circulating liquor radially through the packages

name: Beam Dyeing (concept)
expr: concept: warp yarn or fabric wound on a perforated beam is dyed by circulating liquor through the beam

name: Continuous Dyeing – Pad-Batch (concept)
expr: concept: fabric is padded with dye liquor, batched (rolled), and left to react at room temperature over several hours

name: Continuous Dyeing – Pad-Steam (concept)
expr: concept: fabric is padded with dye liquor and immediately steamed to fix the dye in a continuous process

name: Pad Mangle Expression Percentage (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of liquor retained by fabric after passing through padder nip rollers, controlling dye pick-up

name: Dye Bath pH Control (concept)
expr: concept: dye class and fibre type determine the optimum pH range for maximum exhaustion and level dyeing

name: Levelling Agent (concept)
expr: concept: an auxiliary chemical that controls dye uptake rate to promote even, streak-free dyeing

name: Migration (Dyeing) (concept)
expr: concept: the ability of dye to move within the fibre or fabric after initial uptake, helping correct unlevel dyeing

name: Build-up Property of a Dye (concept)
expr: concept: a dye's ability to reach deeper shades with increasing dye concentration on the fabric

name: Block Printing (concept)
expr: concept: a hand-carved block is dipped in colour paste and pressed onto fabric to create a repeated design

name: Screen Printing (concept)
expr: concept: colour paste is forced through a stencil pattern on a mesh screen onto the fabric below

name: Rotary Screen Printing (concept)
expr: concept: cylindrical perforated screens rotate continuously, allowing high-speed, continuous multi-colour printing

name: Roller (Cylinder) Printing (concept)
expr: concept: engraved copper rollers transfer colour paste directly onto fabric in a continuous high-speed process

name: Digital (Inkjet) Textile Printing (concept)
expr: concept: computer-controlled print heads deposit ink droplets directly onto fabric without a physical screen or roller

name: Transfer (Sublimation) Printing (concept)
expr: concept: disperse dye is printed on paper, then transferred to synthetic fabric using heat and pressure

name: Print Paste Viscosity (concept)
expr: concept: thickener concentration controls print paste viscosity to prevent colour bleeding and ensure sharp designs

name: Thickener Selection (Printing) (concept)
expr: concept: thickener type (e.g. sodium alginate, guar gum) is chosen based on dye class and printing method

name: Print Paste Recipe (concept)
expr: concept: combines dye/pigment, thickener, and auxiliary chemicals in fixed proportions for a target shade and hand feel

name: Steaming (Print Fixation) (concept)
expr: concept: saturated steam provides heat and moisture to fix dye from the printed paste into the fibre

name: Print Registration (concept)
expr: concept: precise alignment of successive colour screens or rollers to avoid overlap or gaps in a multi-colour design

name: Pigment Printing (concept)
expr: concept: colour pigment is bound to the fabric surface with a binder rather than chemically fixed into the fibre

name: Discharge Printing (concept)
expr: concept: a chemical paste locally destroys ground-dyed colour to create a lighter pattern on a dyed background

name: Resist Printing (concept)
expr: concept: a resist paste is printed before dyeing to prevent dye uptake in the printed areas, forming the design

name: Print Colour Fastness (concept)
expr: concept: printed fabric is tested for fastness to washing, rubbing, and light similar to dyed fabric

name: Print Paste Application Method (concept)
expr: concept: application can be by screen, roller, or digital head, each suited to different design complexity and run length

name: Digital Printing Resolution (concept)
expr: concept: print quality on inkjet systems is expressed in dots per inch (DPI), higher DPI giving finer detail

name: Fixation Percentage (Printing) (concept)
expr: concept: the proportion of applied dye or pigment that becomes permanently fixed to the fabric after steaming or curing

name: Colour Matching in Printing (concept)
expr: concept: matching a target shade using a combination of primary dyes/pigments guided by spectrophotometric measurement

name: Print Design Repeat Size (concept)
expr: concept: the dimension after which a printed pattern repeats itself along fabric length and width

name: Calendering (concept)
expr: concept: fabric passes between heated rollers under pressure to smooth, glaze, or emboss its surface

name: Sanforizing (Compressive Shrinkage) (concept)
expr: concept: mechanically compacts fabric to pre-shrink it, reducing residual shrinkage during later washing

name: Raising (Napping) (concept)
expr: concept: fine wire rollers lift fibre ends from the fabric surface to create a soft, fuzzy nap

name: Shearing (Cropping) (concept)
expr: concept: trims raised fibre ends or pile to a uniform, even height after raising or during pile fabric finishing

name: Brushing (Finishing) (concept)
expr: concept: rotating brushes remove loose fibres and lint from the fabric surface after raising or shearing

name: Heat Setting (concept)
expr: concept: thermoplastic fabrics are exposed to controlled heat to stabilize dimensions and set the fabric structure

name: Softening Finish (concept)
expr: concept: chemical softeners are applied to improve fabric hand feel, drape, and surface smoothness

name: Water-Repellent Finish (concept)
expr: concept: a hydrophobic chemical coating causes water to bead and roll off the fabric surface rather than soaking in

name: Waterproof Finish (concept)
expr: concept: a continuous coating or membrane makes fabric fully impermeable to water, unlike a water-repellent finish

name: Flame-Retardant Finish (concept)
expr: concept: chemical treatment reduces a fabric's flammability and slows flame spread

name: Anti-Microbial Finish (concept)
expr: concept: chemical or metallic (e.g. silver-based) treatment inhibits the growth of bacteria and fungi on fabric

name: Wrinkle-Free (Easy-Care) Finish (concept)
expr: concept: cross-linking resin finish improves crease recovery so fabric resists wrinkling after washing and wear

name: UV-Protection Finish (concept)
expr: concept: chemical treatment increases a fabric's Ultraviolet Protection Factor (UPF) by absorbing or reflecting UV rays

name: Anti-Static Finish (concept)
expr: concept: chemical treatment reduces static charge build-up, particularly important for synthetic fibre fabrics

name: Stain-Repellent Finish (concept)
expr: concept: a surface treatment reduces the fabric's tendency to absorb liquid and oil-based stains

name: Fabric Add-on Percentage (Finishing)
expr: Add-on% = ((Weight After Treatment − Weight Before Treatment) / Weight Before Treatment) × 100

name: Pad-Dry-Cure Process (concept)
expr: concept: fabric is padded with a finishing chemical, dried, and then cured at higher temperature to fix the finish permanently

name: Durable Press Finish (concept)
expr: concept: a combination of resin finishing and heat setting to give lasting wrinkle resistance and crease retention

name: Enzyme (Biopolishing) Finish (concept)
expr: concept: cellulase enzymes remove protruding fibrils from cotton fabric surface, giving a smoother, less pilling-prone finish

name: Silicone Softener Treatment (concept)
expr: concept: silicone-based softeners impart a particularly smooth, silky hand feel and improved sewability

name: Fabric Weight Change After Finishing (concept)
expr: concept: finishing treatments can increase or decrease final fabric GSM depending on add-on chemicals and shrinkage

name: Finish Durability (Wash Cycles) (concept)
expr: concept: the number of laundering cycles a finish (e.g. water-repellency) withstands before performance falls below a set threshold

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: CIE L*a*b* Colour Space (concept)
expr: concept: describes colour using lightness (L*) and two colour-opponent dimensions (a* for red-green, b* for yellow-blue)

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Colour Difference (ΔE)
expr: ΔE = √((ΔL*)² + (Δa*)² + (Δb*)²)

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Metamerism (concept)
expr: concept: two colour samples appear to match under one light source but appear different under another

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Whiteness Index (CIE) (concept)
expr: concept: a single numerical value computed from tristimulus values to quantify how white a sample appears

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Yellowness Index (concept)
expr: concept: a numerical value quantifying the degree of yellow discoloration in an otherwise white or near-white material

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Spectrophotometric Colour Matching (concept)
expr: concept: uses reflectance measurements across the visible spectrum to formulate a dye recipe matching a target shade

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Colour Strength (K/S Ratio Comparison) (concept)
expr: concept: comparing K/S values of a sample against a standard to judge relative colour depth

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: ASTM Standards for Textiles (concept)
expr: concept: American Society for Testing and Materials publishes standardized test methods for fibre, yarn, and fabric properties

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: ISO Standards for Textiles (concept)
expr: concept: International Organization for Standardization publishes globally recognized textile testing and terminology standards

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: AATCC Standards for Colourfastness (concept)
expr: concept: American Association of Textile Chemists and Colorists publishes standardized colourfastness and performance test methods

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Oeko-Tex Standard 100 (concept)
expr: concept: an independent certification testing textiles for harmful substances to protect consumer health

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Control Chart Limits (X̄-R Chart)
expr: UCL = X̄̄ + A₂R̄,  LCL = X̄̄ − A₂R̄

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Process Capability Index (Cpk)
expr: Cpk = min[(USL − X̄)/3σ, (X̄ − LSL)/3σ]

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) (concept)
expr: concept: the maximum percentage of defective units in a sampled lot that is considered acceptable for quality control purposes

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Sampling Plan (concept)
expr: concept: defines the sample size and acceptance/rejection criteria used to judge a production lot's quality

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Defect Rate (Quality Control)
expr: Defect Rate% = (Number of Defective Units / Total Units Inspected) × 100

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: First Time Right (FTR) Percentage (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of production passing quality inspection without requiring any rework

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Four-Point Fabric Grading System (concept)
expr: concept: a fabric inspection method assigning penalty points to defects based on their length, used to grade rolls

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Lab Dip Approval (concept)
expr: concept: a small dyed fabric sample submitted for buyer approval before proceeding to bulk dyeing production

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Colour Fastness to Crocking (concept)
expr: concept: measures colour transfer from a fabric to a white test cloth under dry or wet rubbing

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Colour Fastness to Light (concept)
expr: concept: measures fabric colour change after controlled exposure to a standard light source, graded on the Blue Wool Scale

cat: Colour Science, Testing Standards & Quality Control
name: Colour Fastness to Washing (concept)
expr: concept: measures fabric colour change and staining of adjacent fabrics after standardized laundering cycles

name: Marker Efficiency
expr: Marker Efficiency% = (Fabric Area Used by Pattern Pieces / Total Marker Fabric Area) × 100

name: Fabric Consumption per Garment (concept)
expr: concept: total fabric required per garment, estimated from pattern area, marker efficiency, and allowances

name: Lay Length and Ply Height (concept)
expr: concept: the length of a fabric spread (lay) and the number of fabric layers (plies) determine cutting batch size

name: Cutting Wastage Percentage
expr: Cutting Waste% = (Waste Fabric Weight / Total Fabric Weight Used) × 100

name: Stitches Per Inch (SPI) (concept)
expr: concept: the number of stitches formed per inch of seam, affecting seam strength and appearance

name: Seam Efficiency (concept)
expr: concept: the ratio of a sewn seam's breaking strength to the strength of the unsewn fabric

name: Seam Allowance (concept)
expr: concept: the extra fabric width beyond the stitch line included in a pattern piece to allow for sewing

name: Needle Size Selection (concept)
expr: concept: needle size is matched to fabric weight and thread size to avoid skipped stitches or fabric damage

name: Standard Allowed Minute (SAM) (concept)
expr: concept: the standard time, in minutes, allowed to complete one operation or an entire garment under defined conditions

name: Line Efficiency Percentage
expr: Line Efficiency% = ((Output × SAM) / (Total Minutes Worked × Number of Operators)) × 100

name: Production Target per Hour
expr: Target/Hour = (60 / SAM) × Line Efficiency%

name: Work-in-Progress (WIP) (concept)
expr: concept: the quantity of garments that have entered the production line but have not yet completed all operations

name: Line Balancing (concept)
expr: concept: distributing operations among sewing machine operators so that each workstation's cycle time is approximately equal

name: Bottleneck Operation (concept)
expr: concept: the workstation in a sewing line with the longest cycle time, limiting the overall line output rate

name: Cost Per Minute (CM) (concept)
expr: concept: the labour and overhead cost incurred per SAM of production, used as a basis for costing garments

name: CMT (Cut-Make-Trim) Costing (concept)
expr: concept: a garment costing method covering only cutting, sewing, and trimming charges, excluding fabric cost

name: FOB (Free on Board) Price (concept)
expr: concept: the export price of a garment covering all costs up to loading onto the shipping vessel at the port of origin

name: Garment Costing Sheet (concept)
expr: concept: itemizes fabric, trims, CM charges, overheads, and profit margin to arrive at a total garment price

name: Order Quantity vs Efficiency Trade-off (concept)
expr: concept: smaller order quantities typically reduce sewing line efficiency due to more frequent style changeovers

name: On-Time Delivery Percentage (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of shipments dispatched to the buyer within the agreed delivery schedule

name: Capacity Study (concept)
expr: concept: assessing a sewing line or factory's maximum achievable output based on machines, operators, and SAM values

name: Indigo (Rope) Dyeing (concept)
expr: concept: warp yarn ropes are repeatedly dipped and oxidized in indigo dye to build up the characteristic denim surface shade

name: Denim Weight Classification (concept)
expr: concept: denim fabric is classified as light (under 10 oz/yd²), mid (10-14 oz/yd²), or heavy (over 14 oz/yd²)

name: Denim Warp/Weft Construction (concept)
expr: concept: denim is typically a 3/1 or 2/1 twill weave with dyed warp and undyed (grey) weft yarn

name: Stone Washing (concept)
expr: concept: pumice stones are tumbled with denim garments to abrade the surface and create a faded, worn look

name: Enzyme (Bio) Washing (concept)
expr: concept: cellulase enzymes replace or supplement stones to abrade denim surface with less mechanical fabric damage

name: Acid Washing (concept)
expr: concept: pumice stones soaked in a bleaching agent create strong, uneven fading contrast on denim garments

name: Laser Fading (Denim) (concept)
expr: concept: a computer-controlled laser burns away surface indigo dye to create precise, repeatable fade patterns

name: Sanforization (Denim) (concept)
expr: concept: denim fabric is compacted before garment assembly to minimize shrinkage in the finished jeans

name: Geotextile Permittivity (concept)
expr: concept: a measure of how easily water flows perpendicularly through a geotextile fabric, relevant to drainage applications

name: Geotextile Puncture Resistance (concept)
expr: concept: the force required to push a probe through a geotextile fabric, indicating durability under soil loading

name: Geotextile Grab Tensile Strength (concept)
expr: concept: tensile strength measured by gripping only a central portion of the fabric width, simulating localized loading

name: Suture Material Tensile Strength (concept)
expr: concept: medical suture materials are tested for breaking strength and knot-pull strength to ensure surgical reliability

name: Surgical Gown Barrier Performance (concept)
expr: concept: measures a fabric's resistance to liquid and microbial penetration to protect medical staff during procedures

name: Airbag Fabric Properties (concept)
expr: concept: automotive airbag fabric requires high tensile strength, low permeability, and controlled tear propagation

name: Bulletproof (Ballistic) Fabric (concept)
expr: concept: high-tenacity fibres like aramids are woven densely to absorb and disperse the energy of a projectile impact

name: BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) (concept)
expr: concept: the amount of oxygen consumed by microorganisms to break down organic matter in textile mill effluent

name: COD (Chemical Oxygen Demand) (concept)
expr: concept: the amount of oxygen required to chemically oxidize pollutants in textile mill wastewater

name: Water Consumption per kg of Fabric (concept)
expr: concept: total process water used (scouring, bleaching, dyeing, washing) per kilogram of fabric produced

name: Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) (concept)
expr: concept: a series of physical, chemical, and biological treatment stages that clean textile mill wastewater before discharge

name: Carbon Footprint of Textile Processing (concept)
expr: concept: the total greenhouse gas emissions associated with fibre, fabric, and garment production and finishing

name: Water Footprint (Textile Product) (concept)
expr: concept: the total volume of fresh water used directly and indirectly across a textile product's life cycle

name: Recycled Fibre Content Percentage
expr: Recycled Content% = (Weight of Recycled Fibre / Total Fibre Weight) × 100

name: FOB vs CIF Pricing (concept)
expr: concept: FOB covers cost up to the port of origin, while CIF additionally includes freight and insurance to the destination port

name: Quota System (concept)
expr: concept: historical import limits on textile and clothing categories under agreements such as the Multi-Fibre Arrangement

name: GSP Plus Status (concept)
expr: concept: a preferential trade scheme granting reduced or zero tariffs on exports from qualifying developing countries

name: Thick Place (Yarn Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a localized section of yarn with linear density noticeably higher than the surrounding average

name: Thin Place (Yarn Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a localized section of yarn with linear density noticeably lower than the surrounding average, weakening the yarn

name: Neps in Yarn (concept)
expr: concept: small, tightly tangled fibre knots embedded in the yarn body, visible as tiny dark specks in fabric

name: Slub Yarn (concept)
expr: concept: an intentional or unintentional thick, soft section along a yarn's length, sometimes used as a decorative effect

name: Snarl (Yarn Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a small kink or loop formed when a lively, highly twisted yarn twists back on itself

name: Reed Mark (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a fine line defect in fabric caused by a bent, worn, or improperly spaced reed dent

name: Missing End/Pick (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a visible line or gap in fabric caused by a broken warp end or weft pick that was not replaced during weaving

name: Barre Effect (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: visible crosswise streaks in fabric caused by yarn irregularities or uneven dyeing between weft picks

name: Shade Variation (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: visible colour differences within or between fabric rolls caused by inconsistent dyeing conditions

name: Crease Mark (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a permanent fold line defect set into fabric during wet processing or finishing under tension

name: Oil/Stain Mark (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: localized discoloration caused by machine oil, grease, or other contamination during processing

name: Weft Bar (Fabric Fault) (concept)
expr: concept: a horizontal band of different appearance across the fabric width caused by weft yarn or tension irregularity

name: Value Addition in Textile Chain (concept)
expr: concept: the increase in product value at each stage from raw fibre through yarn, fabric, and finished garment

name: Textile Export Share (concept)
expr: concept: the proportion of a country's total export earnings contributed by textile and apparel products

name: Organic Cotton Certification (concept)
expr: concept: certifies cotton grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers, verified through a chain-of-custody standard

name: Absenteeism Rate (Garment Factory) (concept)
expr: concept: the percentage of scheduled workers who are absent on a given production day, affecting planned output

name: Man-Made vs Cotton Fibre Consumption Ratio (concept)
expr: concept: the relative share of synthetic/regenerated fibres versus cotton in a country's or the world's total fibre use
